title: Phase-switchable nonreciprocal entanglement via magnon squeezing in ring-cavity optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, I. P. Castillo
abstract: Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting phase-controlled magnon squeezing. Indeed, two spatially separated ferrimagnetic YIG microbridges become entangled through their magnetostriction-mediated coupling to mechanical motion and a common cavity field via radiation-pressure interaction. The squeezing process introduces two phase-dependent contributions to the magnon response, namely an effective detuning shift $Δ_{θ_j}$ and a quadrature-damping contribution $κ_{θ_j}$, both of which reverse sign upon a $π$ phase shift, providing an in situ control to switch the entanglement response. The nonreciprocal entanglement is defined operationally through the asymmetric entanglement response under the phase reversal $θ_j \to θ_j + π$, quantified by normalized contrast ratios $C_E$ and $C_{\mathcal{R}}$, which measure the relative difference between the entanglement obtained at $θ_j$ and at the phase-reversed configuration $θ_j+π$. The resulting phase-tuning method provides a flexible and robust route to achieve high-contrast bipartite and tripartite entanglement within stable parameter regions, establishing magnon squeezing as a practical quantum resource for switchable quantum correlations in hybrid platforms.
summary: The paper proposes using magnon squeezing in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity to generate switchable, nonreciprocal bipartite and tripartite entanglement. By controlling the phase of the magnon squeezing, researchers can reverse key system parameters, offering a robust method to tune quantum correlations without physical reconfiguration. This establishes magnon squeezing as a powerful, controllable resource for advanced quantum information processing in solid-state systems.
main_problem: The goal is to generate and control switchable nonreciprocal entanglement using magnon squeezing within a cavity optomagnomechanical system.
main_result: The proposed phase-tuning method successfully demonstrates high-contrast, switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement by exploiting the sign reversal of effective detuning and damping rates upon a $\pi$ phase shift.
method: The theoretical framework involves linearizing quantum Langevin equations around steady states to analyze fluctuations, followed by calculating entanglement measures like logarithmic negativity and residual contangle.
model_or_system: The system is an optomagnomechanical ring cavity coupling two ferrimagnetic YIG microbridges (magnons) to a common optical cavity mode and mechanical oscillators. The dynamics are governed by a complex Hamiltonian involving various detunings, couplings, and the phase-controlled magnon squeezing terms.
key_observables: Nonreciprocal entanglement is quantified using normalized contrast ratios ($C_E$ and $C_{\mathcal{R}}$), while bipartite entanglement uses logarithmic negativity ($E^N$) and tripartite entanglement uses residual contangle ($R^N$).
important_parameters: The control mechanism relies on the phase ($	heta_j$) of the magnon squeezing, which dictates the sign reversal of effective detuning shifts ($\Delta	heta_j$) and quadrature-damping contributions ($\kappa_{	heta j}$). Stability analysis is crucial, requiring all eigenvalues of the drift matrix to have negative real parts.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a low-excitation regime for magnon populations and neglects bending-related displacements in the mechanical modes. Furthermore, stability requires operating within parameter regimes where the Routh–Hurwitz criterion is satisfied.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical platform and Hamiltonian, then derives the linearized quantum Langevin equations. It proceeds to analyze stability conditions using Routh–Hurwitz criteria before calculating entanglement measures (logarithmic negativity/residual contangle) and demonstrating the phase-switchable nonreciprocity.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it merges concepts from cavity QED, magnonics, and optomechanics to create a controllable quantum resource. The ability to switch entanglement using only a phase shift ($	heta 	o 	heta+\pi$) provides an advanced degree of tunability for hybrid quantum platforms.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly models magnons (spin waves) coupled to an optical cavity mode within a solid-state system (YIG microbridges), fitting the description of magnon/photon polaritons and quantum-optical descriptions of magnetic systems.
